claim: For the Caputo SEIAR system of Sene and Mansal, the model and the authors' own component definitions require the asymptomatic and recovered Volterra equations to be \(A(t)=A(0)+I^\alpha F_4(t,y)\) and \(R(t)=R(0)+I^\alpha F_5(t,y)\). The printed numerical derivation instead writes \(A(t_n)=A(0)+I^\alpha F_3(t_n,y)\) and \(R(t_n)=R(0)+I^\alpha F_4(t_n,y)\), and the displayed corrector formulas repeat exactly those two shifted right-hand sides; the recovered predictor also uses \(F_4\) rather than \(F_5\). This is a structural component-indexing error, not a harmless notation change. For any consistent quadrature applied to the printed mapping, the small-step limit solves the wrong two Volterra equations whenever \(F_3\ne F_4\) or \(F_4\ne F_5\), so the paper's stated \(O(h^{\min\{\alpha+1,2\}})\) errors for \(A\) and \(R\) and its conclusion that all five printed approximations converge to the exact SEIAR model cannot hold as written. An exact admissible witness is \(\theta=1/2\), \(\rho=2\), \(\gamma=\mu=\omega=\tau=1\) with \(E(0)=1\) and \(I(0)=A(0)=R(0)=0\): then \(F_3(0)=1/2\), \(F_4(0)=1\), and \(F_5(0)=0\), so for every \(0<\alpha\le1\) the target and printed integral equations differ at leading order by \(-t^\alpha/(2\Gamma(\alpha+1))\) in \(A\) and by \(+t^\alpha/\Gamma(\alpha+1)\) in \(R\). The finding concerns the equations and convergence claims as printed; it does not establish which component mapping, if any, was used in unpublished source code or in the paper's plotted simulations.
integrity: The component mapping was reconstructed directly from the open-access article and compared with the article's own earlier Volterra equations and later right-hand-side definitions. A rational witness verifies that the shifted fields are genuinely distinct. The general Garrappa formulation was inspected to confirm that system quadrature applies the supplied vector field componentwise.
scientific_limitations: The result concerns the equations and convergence statements as printed. No public source code was located, so it does not determine whether the figures were generated with corrected component indices. It does not assess a repaired implementation or the article's separate equilibrium and stability analysis.
title: A repeated component-indexing error invalidates two printed SEIAR convergence claims
